news.title: 'Falklands issue was a special ingredient': Lautaro lifts lid on Argentina’s World Cup grudge match against England
news.lede: Lautaro Martinez has revealed how Argentina’s long-running dispute with England over the Falkland Islands added an emotional edge to their 2026 World Cup semifinal, describing the clash as far more than a football match and dedicating his decisive goal to veterans of the 1982 war. The Inter Milan striker scored a 92nd-minute winner as Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 in Atlanta on July 15, booking their place in a second consecutive World Cup final. The goal has since taken on a significance beyond the result, particularly among Argentines who continue to regard the conflict over the islands as a defining chapter in their national history. In an interview with AFA Estudio, Martinez became emotional when shown footage of a Malvinas War veteran breaking down in tears while celebrating his goal.

news.title: Ronaldo and other veterans still going strong ahead of 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is expected to showcase the sport’s next generation of stars, but several players in their 40s are still competing at the highest international level. When the tournament kicks off across the United States, Canada and Mexico, these veteran names will not just be making up the numbers. From experienced goalkeepers to former Ballon d’Or winners, each is still expected to play an important role for their respective countries on football’s biggest stage. Perhaps surprisingly, Nagatomo was called up by Japan head coach Hajime Moriyasu despite his limited involvement with the national team in recent years.

news.title: How to Watch the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Morocco 2026™
news.lede: Australia secured its historic qualification at the AFC U-17 Women’s Asian Cup China 2026™ with a 2-0 quarter-final victory over Vietnam, before the team went on to finish fourth at the tournament. The FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Morocco 2026™ will run from 17 October to 7 November 2026, with Australia drawn into Group F alongside Spain, Mexico and Chile. All matches involving the CommBank Junior Matildas will be shown live on Paramount+ in Australia; find out how to watch around the rest of the world.

news.title: 5 Southeast Asian-based players going to 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is set to bring together the world’s best players across the United States, Canada and Mexico from June 11 to July 19. While no Southeast Asian national team managed to qualify for the expanded 48-team tournament, the region will still have a presence on football’s biggest stage through several players currently plying their trade in the region. Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia are all represented, with Selangor, Terengganu, Port FC and Persib Bandung contributing players to World Cup squads. Several others also came close to securing places before final selections were announced.

news.title: Five-time world champions Nigeria miss fourth straight U17 World Cup
news.lede: The five-time world champions saw their qualification hopes fade following a 1-1 draw against Ivory Coast in Burkina Faso on Saturday. Having suffered a 2-1 defeat to Niger Republic in their opening fixture, The Golden Eaglets needed victory against the Ivorians to keep their qualification ambitions alive. However, coach Eboboritse Uwejamomere's team could only manage a draw, finishing bottom of their three-team group and consequently missing out on qualification for the 2027 U17 Africa Cup of Nations and FIFA U17 World Cup. The latest setback represents another painful chapter in the decline of a country widely regarded as one of the greatest forces in youth international football.

news.title: Infantino in Morocco: praise and a message before the 2030 World Cup
news.lede: A new stop before the dream World Cup. Gianni Infantino is back in Morocco. The FIFA president timed his visit to coincide with the start of the Under-17 Women's World Cup "Morocco 2026", praising Moroccans' passion for football at a time when the Kingdom is preparing to host the biggest event of all in partnership with Spain and Portugal in 2030. Royal Moroccan Football Federation president Fouzi Lekjaa received Infantino for the tournament's opening ceremony and the opening match, another sign of Morocco's growing standing as a host of international competitions.
